goal: The first frame of the game. The two items SPAWN-YAW left in not_done: the census hand-back framing (the wall of reed-cases at the instant control returns, before any door) and the collapsed camera arm at the writ-house doorstep (the player not in the first controlled frame).
done: MEASURED IN BARE NODE, not a browser: tools/harness/opening-frame.mjs imports the shipped modules (WorldField, planSettlement/settlementSolids, CollisionCell, exitFacing, CENSUS_PLACES) and runs sim/camera.js stepCamera() ITSELF, 60 fixed steps on a real SimState. No frame budget to miss, so contention cannot fabricate a defect. Metric for 'the player is not in the frame' is the game's own: camera.charOpacity, which fadeOpacity() drives to 0 at arm <= 0.90 m.

DEFECT 2 DIAGNOSED, AND IT IS NOT A TREE AND NOT A FACING. The arm's cast lands in writ-house:+z+ 0.20 m behind the pivot. The writ-house footprint (x 3801.0-3811.0, z 895.5-908.5) and the barge-hold footprint (x 3792.0-3808.0, z 904.5-911.5) OVERLAP BY 7.02 x 4.00 m; the writ house's front door opens inside the barge hold and the doorstep is the 0.6 m corner pocket left over — 0.67 m from one wall, 0.41 m from the other.

THE FULL NUMBER LINE (HAZARDS 0b): all 72 five-degree bearings scored through the real stepCamera. Perfectly bimodal, no middle. 25/72 keep the player drawn; best drawn bearing sees 0.75 m; best-seeing bearing (12 m) draws no player. NO FACING RULE CAN FIX THIS STANDING POINT.

DEFECT 1 FIXED, and the diagnosis in the dispatch was half right: the camera yaw was 6.6 deg off the doorway in a 79.3 deg FOV — the way out was already on screen. What was wrong was DRAWN GEOMETRY. render/places.js#buildWritHouse() drew the +z wall as one unbroken 11 m slab: the room had NO DOOR IN IT AT ALL, while interiorShellPlan() cut a 1.40 x 2.10 doorway there and the world door stands on that face. The reed-cases (8.2 m, four rows) then stood 0.6 m in front of it.

FIX. Engine._censusHandBack() turns body AND combat mirror AND sim.camera.yaw (all three, or it is inert) to the way out on the frame the census graph runs out of nodes, re-solves the spring arm and re-quantises cold state; character/scene.js#doorwayLocal()/handBackFraming() resolve the doorway from bounds_m + entry_side, restating interiorShellPlan()'s arithmetic so character/ does not depend on render/; fails open with engine.censusHandBack.applied saying so. places.js cuts the doorway, adds frame + named leaf, splits the reed-cases into two runs around it, narrows the window to fit the gap.

MEASURED, ray-classified against the DRAWN meshes with the BEFORE arm imported straight out of git (--baseline 8361fcb9), not retyped: doorway visible 0% -> 57% at the shipped camera yaw and 0% -> 69% at the fixed yaw. Before is zero on every arm because there was no door to see; every ray stopped on the 11.00x4.00x0.35 wall slab or the shelving. Walking straight forward: as-shipped body yaw 320 MISSES the doorway by 2.64 m, fixed reaches it.

NULL CONTROL is the plausible wrong answer (body + combat mirror written, sim.camera.yaw not) and it earns its keep at the doorstep: arm 3.993 m, char_opacity 100%, clearance 0.25 m — a perfectly framed player looking at a wall. At the hand-back it separates by only 12 points (57 vs 69) and that is reported as such rather than dressed up.

TWO MEASUREMENT ARTEFACTS FOUND IN MY OWN TOOL AND WRITTEN INTO IT: a sample plane at z=6.30 scored the FIXED room 0% (rays terminating inside the door the fix added); moving it to 6.15 moved an unchanged arm by 43 points (the raycaster's far epsilon eating shelf hits 0.03 m in front). Replaced by 'what does the ray hit FIRST', with the door meshes named in the scene graph.

EVIDENCE. Two hardware runs, NVIDIA L4 and RTX A5000, ANGLE/Vulkan, software_renderer:false. 62 frames each: desktop 1280x720 and phone 390x844, title/barge-hold/hand-back, an 8-angle orbit AROUND THE HAND-BACK FRAME (new — opening-capture.mjs only orbited the doorstep before), the doorstep orbit, and 10 s of walking. Viewports verified to differ by PNG dimensions and md5, not by a check going green. Per-frame arm_m / char_opacity / arm_guard now in the manifest.
TWO PODS RENTED, $0.023 and $0.024, BOTH terminated with API-confirmed deletion (subsequent API lookup returned not found). Nothing left billing.
not_done: THE DOORSTEP DEFECT IS NOT FIXED. It cannot be fixed by a facing and the dispatch forbids moving where the player stands ('Fix what the player is looking at, not where they are'). It needs a ruling: either separate thorn.json's writ-house and barge-hold (they are 7x4 m inside each other — the root cause) or push continuity.exterior_spawn ~3.5 m along the door's outward normal, which needs 4.4 m of free space behind the body and has 0.41 m. OVERTURNED BY: opening-frame.mjs reporting sweep_summary.best_drawn_and_clear with clearance_m above about 6 m.

The building overlap was found at Thorn and NOT audited across the other seven towns. planSettlement() returns no deep_overlaps/shrunk field on this record at all, so 'how many buildings in this world are inside each other' is open and is a one-tool answer.

buildWritHouse() has one lamp and it is at z=-4, the far end from the door. A second lamp was deliberately NOT added: the file records a shared policy that this room takes litLights()'s fail-open hearth rather than private lamps. If the doorway end reads too dark, that policy is what to revisit.

writ-house.json's continuity.interior_spawn is [0,0,-4.6], against the -z wall, 11 m from the +z doorway — the same entry_side/interior_spawn contradiction settlement.js documents on 109 of 115 records. Named in the tool's output; not touched, it is the door placement's field.
The deployed Pages URL was not tested; Chromium here still cannot reach any external host. Everything measured on the local tree.

The reed-case gap, the door frame and the window width are a first pass judged from hardware frames at two viewports, not against a Thorn art-direction target — Thorn still has zero composition-valid reference plates (docs/art-direction/ART.md, n=0).
